correctness.rationale: Set a=qM+r with 1<=r<M, gcd(r,M)=1. Reconstructed T(a/M)=q(M+r)/M, first reduced denominator d=M/gcd(q,M); exact order two iff d>1 and d divides Q=q+floor(qr/M), where q<=Q<=2q-1. The quotient-exclusion cases for k=2s, k=2s+1 at p odd, and k odd at p=2 rule out every smaller q using p-adic valuation and d>Q. For odd p, the candidate q=p^s(p+1)/2 requires Q=p^(s+1), fixing the minimal r0=ceil[M(p-1)/(p+1)]; modular calculation proves p does not divide r0. Even-exponent and odd binary choices use r=1. Directly checked M=2 special mu=7. An independent fresh exact Fraction enumeration verified candidates and excluded 83714 smaller coprime numerators for 32 prime-power cases <=1000, while the all-prime proof is the quotient/divisibility argument, not this enumeration.
